text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.66% today as crude oil prices dropped for a second consecutive day on hopes for a diplomatic resolution to the Iran conflict. The stock had surged over $7 on October 30th when geopolitical tensions appeared to be escalating, but news of potential U.S.-Iran negotiations and Democrats winning the midterms — a party historically less supportive of oil and gas — triggered a sharp reversal. The sell-off reflects a straightforward reality: as the risk of war diminishes, the premium investors had priced into oil stocks evaporates.

The broader context matters here: crude hit $103.37 per barrel today, down from levels that had climbed as geopolitical risk spiked. A Democratic Congress is expected to favor renewable energy over fossil fuels, adding headwinds to the sector beyond just the immediate Iran situation. For an oil company like ConocoPhillips, peace and a political shift toward renewables both work in the same direction—lower prices and less favorable policy tailwinds.
